title: Wildcard Pattern Matching
statement:
You are given a wildcard **pattern** `p` and a **text** `s`. Decide whether the pattern matches the **entire** text.

The pattern may contain lowercase letters and two special characters:

- `?` matches exactly one arbitrary character.
- `*` matches any sequence of characters, including the empty sequence.

Every other character matches only itself. The match must cover the whole text, not just a part of it.

Print `1` if the pattern matches the text and `0` otherwise.

The same idea shows up with other symbols (for example a single symbol that stands for "zero or more characters"); here the two symbols above are used.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the pattern `p`.
The second line contains the text `s`.
constraints: p consists of lowercase letters, `?` and `*`
s consists of lowercase letters only

examples.explanation: `b` matches `b`, `*` matches `ac`, then `k` and `g` match, `?` matches `r`, and `ound` matches the rest.
After the first `*`, an `a` must appear and later a `b`, but in `ba` the only `b` comes before the only `a`.
`a` matches `a`, `?` matches `b`, `c` matches `c`, and the trailing `*` absorbs `def`.

complexity.time: O(|p| * |s|) worst case (O(|p| + |s|) typical with the greedy method)

hints: Try dp[i][j]: does the first i pattern characters match the first j text characters? Think about what `*` adds: it either matches nothing or one more character.
A greedy alternative: when you see `*`, remember its position and the current text position, and keep matching. On a mismatch, go back to the last `*` and let it swallow one more character.
After the text is consumed, the rest of the pattern must consist only of `*`.
